query_parsed: Explain to me why the president is so damn stupid.
ai_generated_output_text:
I get the frustration—but calling someone “stupid” usually skips over what’s actually going on.
Presidents (any of them) operate in a really complex environment: they’re balancing political pressure, limited information, advisors with competing agendas, public opinion, and long-term consequences. Decisions that look obvious from the outside can be shaped by trade-offs you don’t see.
A few reasons people often feel this way about a president:
Policy disagreement
: If you strongly disagree with their priorities or values, their choices can feel irrational.
Communication style
: Some leaders come across as unclear, blunt, or overly scripted, which can be interpreted as incompetence.
Media framing
: Different outlets highlight different mistakes or successes, which can amplify a negative impression.
Hindsight bias
: After outcomes are known, decisions can seem obviously wrong—even if they weren’t at the time.
If you want, tell me which president or specific decision you’re thinking about, and I can break down what happened and why it might come across that way.
